title: wt sync move --json
description: What `wt sync move --json` prints on stdout: one object, for a move! commit written or refused. A refusal has a null commit, writes nothing and exits non-zero; a command line wt cannot read prints no object and exits non-zero. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows.

work.description: The worktree as it was named.

branch.description: The worktree's branch, whose top the commit goes on; null when the worktree was not found.

message.description: The whole message: the move! subject and the Move-From, Move-Path and Move-Lines lines.

commit.description: The move! commit written, now the branch's tip; null when none was written.

from.description: The commit --from names on the line; null when it names none, more than one, or the line was not read.

into.description: The commit --into names on the line; null as for from.

paths.description: The paths moved whole, as given; for a commit written, each once.

lines.description: The line ranges moved, as given; for a commit written, each once.

refusal.description: Why no commit was written, in the words printed on stderr; null when one was.

lineRange.description: Lines from to to, inclusive, of path as the source commit leaves it: the move takes every hunk of the source's diff of path the range overlaps.
